\chapter{Complexity — Oracle}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Oracle
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module defines oracle Turing machines in the sense of Arora--Barak
(Definition~3.4): multi-tape machines with one designated query tape and three
designated states, where entering the query state submits the query tape's
contents to an oracle language and moves, in a single step, to a positive- or
negative-answer state.  It provides the step and run semantics relative to an
oracle, a time-bounded computation predicate, basic locality invariants of
initialized runs (head positions and blank cells, bounding the query length),
and two lockstep sanity checks for the architecture: every plain machine embeds
as an oracle machine whose behavior is oracle-independent, and conversely every
oracle machine run with the empty oracle is eliminated into a plain machine.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Oracle Turing machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002
}
\label{Turing.OracleTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
An oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes over a symbol alphabet
$\Sigma$ and state set $Q$ consists of an initial state $q_0$, a designated
query state $q_{\mathrm{query}}$, a designated positive-answer state
$q_{\mathrm{yes}}$, a designated negative-answer state $q_{\mathrm{no}}$, and a
transition function that assigns to every state, scanned input symbol
(possibly blank), and family of scanned symbols on the $k+1$ work tapes (the
last of which serves as the query tape) a one-step action on the $k+1$ work
tapes.  The transition function governs every state except the query state,
whose behavior is instead determined by the oracle.  The structure itself does
not require the three special states to be distinct; that is imposed
separately by well-formedness.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Well-formed oracle machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM}
An oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes is well formed when its
three special states are pairwise distinct: the query state differs from the
positive-answer state, the query state differs from the negative-answer state,
and the two answer states differ from each other.  The initial state is
allowed to coincide with the query state (such a machine submits the empty
query on its first step).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Index of the query tape]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
\leanok
For an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, the index of the query
tape among the $k+1$ work tapes: the last index, $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Query string of a configuration]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryString}
\statementsource{BGS75}{pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryString}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
For a configuration of a machine with $k+1$ work tapes over an alphabet
$\Sigma$, the query string is the word read off the query tape (the last work
tape) from cell $0$ rightward, up to but excluding the first blank cell.  If
no cell at a nonnegative position of the query tape is blank --- possible for
an arbitrary configuration, though not for one reachable from an initial
configuration --- the query string is defined to be the empty word.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One step relative to an oracle]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step}
\statementsource{BGS75}{pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.queryString}
One step of an oracle machine $M$ with $k$ ordinary work tapes relative to an
oracle language $O$ over the alphabet $\Sigma$, acting on a configuration $c$
with $k+1$ work tapes.  A halted configuration is left fixed.  If the current
state is the query state, the machine moves to the positive-answer state when
the query string of $c$ belongs to $O$ and to the negative-answer state
otherwise, with all tapes, head positions, and the output left unchanged.  In
every other state, the machine applies the action prescribed by its transition
function for the current state and the scanned input and work-tape symbols,
exactly like a plain multi-tape machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial configuration of an oracle machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.initCfg}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.initCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.OracleTM}
The initial configuration of an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes on
a given input word: the machine is in its initial state, the input head is at
the origin, all $k+1$ work tapes (including the query tape) are blank with
their heads at the origin, and the output is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Run of an oracle machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.step}
The configuration reached by running an oracle machine $M$ with oracle $O$ for
$t$ steps from a configuration $c$: the $t$-fold iterate of the one-step
function of $M$ relative to $O$, applied to $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Time-bounded oracle computation]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom}
An oracle machine $M$ with oracle $O$ computes the word $y$ on input $x$
within $t$ steps when, after running $M$ relative to $O$ for $t$ steps from
its initial configuration on $x$, the machine has halted and its output tape
holds exactly $y$.  This is a time-only notion; space is not constrained.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Step Independence Away from the Query State]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O_1,O_2$ be languages over its symbol
alphabet, and let $c$ be a configuration. If the state of $c$ is not the query state of
$M$, then one step from $c$ relative to $O_1$ equals one step from $c$ relative to
$O_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Extension of an action by an inert tape]
\lean{Turing.Action.extend}
\label{Turing.Action.extend}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
The extension of a one-step action on $k$ work tapes to an action on $k+1$
work tapes: on the first $k$ tapes it writes and moves exactly as before, and
on the extra last tape it writes nothing and does not move the head.  The
input-head move, the output emission, and the next state are unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding of a configuration for the oracle model]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle}
\label{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
The embedding of a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes and state
set $Q$ into a configuration of a machine with $k+1$ work tapes over the
extended state set $Q \sqcup \{0,1,2\}$: the state (if the machine has not
halted) is renamed along the left inclusion, the input head, the first $k$
work tapes with their head positions, and the output are unchanged, and the
extra last work tape is blank with its head at the origin.
\end{definition}

alphabet, let $x$ be an input word over $\Sigma$, and let $c$ be a configuration with

head of the embedded configuration equals the optional symbol scanned by the input head

\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Plain machine as an oracle machine that never queries]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.extend, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM}
The embedding of a plain multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes and state set
$Q$ as an oracle machine over the extended state set $Q \sqcup \{0,1,2\}$: the
three fresh states serve as the query, positive-answer, and negative-answer
states, the initial state is the image of the original initial state, and on
original states the transition function is the original transition (renamed
along the left inclusion and extended by an inert query tape), so that the
machine never moves into a fresh state and ignores the query tape.  From each
of the three fresh states the transition table halts immediately.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Well-formedness of the embedded machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM_wellFormed}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM_wellFormed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed, Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes. Regard it as an oracle
Turing machine with state set formed by adjoining three fresh states, designated as the
query state and the positive- and negative-answer states. The resulting oracle machine
is well formed: its query state and two answer states are pairwise distinct.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Empty-oracle elimination]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM}
Given an oracle machine $M$ with $k$ ordinary work tapes and state set $Q$,
the plain multi-tape machine with $k+1$ work tapes over the same state set $Q$
that simulates $M$ run with the empty oracle: it has the same initial state,
and its transition function agrees with that of $M$ in every state except the
query state, where it instead performs a stationary move (no writes, no head
movement, no output) directly into the negative-answer state, since the empty
oracle always answers no.
\end{definition}

\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_plainEmptyOracle}

\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, and let $c$ be a
configuration with $k+1$ work tapes. The successor of $c$ under the plain machine
obtained from $M$ by the empty-oracle elimination is equal to the successor of $c$ under
$M$ with the empty oracle.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_plainEmptyOracle}

\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_comm_of_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ and $M'$ be oracle Turing machines, with oracle languages $O$ and $O'$,
respectively. Suppose a map $f$ from configurations of $M$ to configurations of $M'$
satisfies $M'$'s one-step update with oracle $O'$ at $f(c)$ equals $f$ of $M$'s one-step
update with oracle $O$, for every configuration $c$. Then, for every configuration $c$
and every nonnegative integer $n$, running $M'$ from $f(c)$ for $n$ steps yields $f$ of
the configuration obtained by running $M$ from $c$ for $n$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Runs agree before any query]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_forall_ne_qQuery}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_forall_ne_qQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ and $O'$ be oracle languages, and let $c$
be a configuration. Suppose that at every time $s<t$, the run from $c$ using oracle $O$
is not in the query state. Then the configurations reached after $t$ steps using $O$ and
$O'$ are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-step tape radius bound]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_radius}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step_radius}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.workTapePos_step_le, Turing.OracleTM.workTapes_step_eq_of_ne}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $O$ be an oracle
language, and let $c$ be a configuration with $k+1$ work tapes. Choose a work-tape index
$i$ and a natural number $n$. If the head on tape $i$ is at distance at most $n$ from
the origin, and every cell $z$ with $|z|\ge n$ on that tape is blank, then after one
step relative to $O$ the head on tape $i$ is at distance at most $n+1$ from the origin,
and every cell $z$ with $|z|\ge n+1$ on that tape is blank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Work-tape support radius after a run]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_radius}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_radius}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.OracleTM.step_radius}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $O$ be a language over
its symbol alphabet, and let $c$ be a configuration with $k+1$ work tapes. Fix a tape
$i$ and a natural number $n$. Suppose the absolute value of the head position on tape
$i$ in $c$ is at most $n$, and every cell $z$ on that tape with $n\le |z|$ is blank.
Then for every $s\in\mathbb{N}$, after running $M$ relative to $O$ for $s$ steps, the
head position on tape $i$ has absolute value at most $n+s$, and every cell $z$ with
$n+s\le |z|$ is blank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query length bounded by a blank cell]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le_of_blank}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le_of_blank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c$ be a configuration with $k+1$ work tapes, and let $n$ be a natural number. If
the query-tape cell at position $n$ is blank, then the query string of $c$ has length at
most $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query string determined by its cells]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_eq_of_cells}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_eq_of_cells}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
\difficulty{6}
Let $c$ be a configuration with $k+1$ work tapes and let $w$ be a finite word. Suppose
that at each position $i$ with $0\le i<|w|$, the query tape contains the $i$-th symbol
of $w$, and that the cell at position $|w|$ is blank. Then the query string of $c$ is
$w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Agreement with the empty-oracle simulation]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_plainEmptyOracle}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_plainEmptyOracle}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_forall_ne_qQuery, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_plainEmptyOracle}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle language, and let $c$ be a
configuration. Suppose that at every time $s<t$, the run from $c$ by the plain machine
simulating $M$ with the empty oracle is not in the query state. Then the configuration
reached after $t$ steps by running $M$ with oracle $O$ from $c$ equals the configuration
reached after $t$ steps by that plain machine.
\end{theorem}
